Every citation on a mover, volume outlier, or recommendation card carries the actual publish date of its source, separate from this page's pull date above. Price/volume/index data always refreshes live on pull; narrative research is only rewritten when genuinely newer reporting was found for that name - otherwise the existing writeup stands rather than being re-presented under a fresher-looking timestamp. The 10/24/26 pull (a Saturday) reflects the Friday Oct 23 session - equity data is current through that close, with no data lag. Unlike the Oct 16 session's single sector-wide selloff, Friday's movers are mostly company-specific Q3 earnings and guidance stories, with three cross-cutting themes. First, a Bloomberg report that SpaceX is negotiating for at least 80,000 U.S. tower sites lifted tower owners (Crown Castle, American Tower, SBA) and hit carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, ~-8% each); no lease is signed. Second, Brent's settle at $116.72 (a six-month high) lifted oilfield-service names (Schlumberger on its own Q3 beat; Noble, Tidewater, Oceaneering and Innovex mostly on crude). Third, consumer-credit names fell after Sallie Mae cut 2026 guidance and raised charge-off guidance (SLM -10.8%; Enova and FirstCash also fell, with coverage citing weak consumer-credit peers). The largest single moves are earnings-driven: Robert Half +21.7% (staffing revenue growth returned), LKQ -22.5% (pre-announced Q3 miss, guidance withdrawn, CEO out), Corcept -20.1% (a competitor's ovarian-cancer Phase 3 win). Cybersecurity names (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto) rose on an Evercore ISI channel survey, and Instacart rose on an unconfirmed report of early sale talks. Dave, Newell Brands, Tootsie Roll and Innovex turned up no clean catalyst despite a genuine search and are marked that way. Bounce-screen names (Carpenter, Comfort Systems, Graco, Howmet, ATI, Sterling, Flex, IES) mostly fell in the Oct 22 AI-infrastructure/aerospace selloff or on their own earnings. Existing writeups updated with dated news: Liquidia (Oct 13 litigation settlement with United Therapeutics), Five9, Enova, Arcus (Oct 21 equity offering), Flex, IES, and the Fiserv value card; AppLovin, Insulet and CoStar had nothing new and stand as of 10/18/26. The $2B market-cap filter was refreshed on 10/24/26, which moved Kaiser Aluminum below the line (and out of the losers and bounce lists) and brought in Newell Brands, Tootsie Roll, Innovex and SBA.

CRS — Carpenter Technology Updated

Industrials ▸
aligned

A defensible but not clean bounce candidate. The selloff punished a revenue/cash-flow timing miss, not a broken story: margins were record (SAO adjusted margin 37.7%), aerospace structural/distribution bookings rose 49% y/y, Q2 operating-income guidance ($192-197M) implies +24-27% y/y, FY2027 and the FY2029 $1.2-1.3B operating-income target were reaffirmed, and the company launched a new $1B buyback after repurchasing $133.9M in the quarter. Against that: full-year FCF guidance ($400-430M) now requires a big back-half catch-up after a negative Q1, the stock was richly valued before the drop, and it has been de-rating since summer (52-week high ~$626). A bounce needs evidence that the maintenance-hit volumes return in Q2; until then, treat as a high-beta mean-reversion trade rather than value.

CORT — Corcept Therapeutics Incorporated Updated

Health Care ▸
aligned

Mixed bounce case. Lifyorli is already approved and on the market, while Rina-S has not been filed. Corcept therefore keeps a commercial window, likely measured in years, and its core cortisol-modulator business (Korlym in Cushing's syndrome) is unaffected by Friday's news. Against that, the Rina-S data are strong enough that oncologists may switch once it is approved, so the ovarian-cancer opportunity behind much of the 2026 rerating has a shorter shelf life. Also, the relacorilant hypercortisolism NDA got a CRL in Dec 2025. The 20% drop reprices a real competitive threat; it is not noise. Any bounce depends on Q3 results (late Oct / early Nov) showing Lifyorli launch traction.

LKQ — LKQ Corporation Updated

Consumer Discretionary ▸
aligned

A real but early bounce candidate. In favor: North America, the larger and steadier business, came in line. The damage is concentrated in a self-inflicted European ERP and execution problem that Alvarez & Marsal and new management can, in principle, fix. And the stock is near multi-year lows after the ~22% drop. Against: guidance is withdrawn, so there is no earnings floor. The Oct 29 full report and call could bring more detail on Europe. A new CEO starting Dec 15 often 'kitchen-sinks' the next guide. The ERP problem has now spanned two quarters, which suggests it is not a one-off. Treat it as a speculative turnaround bounce, not a mean-reversion trade on noise, and wait for the Oct 29 numbers before sizing.

FCFS — FirstCash Updated

Financials ▸
counter

A sensible bounce candidate. The selloff punishes valuation and a shrinking non-core segment, not the core business. Pawn, the large majority of profits, grew strongly in both the U.S. and Latin America, and pawn demand tends to rise when lower-income consumers are stretched, which is the same stress that hit Sallie Mae Friday. AFF credit actually improved (monthly net charge-offs 5.6% vs 5.8%). The company is buying back stock ($123M in Q3 at ~$209 average, above today's price) and raised its dividend. Risks: AFF is guided to keep shrinking through Q4, only $50M of buyback authorization is left, and part of the premium multiple may not come back. The case rests on pawn growth continuing to offset AFF.

APP — AppLovin No update

Communication Services ▸
counter

The overhang deepened: Goldman Sachs cut its price target to $400 from $465 (Neutral) on Oct 14, and Benzinga/Defense World report shares hit a new 52-week low that week (~$258-263) amid the tech selloff and the pending class actions (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 16). Trailing P/E has compressed to ~20x per GuruFocus. Q3 results Nov 4 are the next resolution point. No change to the 'explained discount, not a mystery' read. AppLovin's discount is well-explained, not a mystery: shares are down roughly 54% in 2026 after a narrow Q2 revenue miss ($1.92B vs. $1.94B consensus) triggered analyst downgrades, followed by a mid-September securities class action alleging AppLovin overstated its AI model progress and didn't fully disclose delays to a planned generative-AI video tool. Competitive pressure from Meta's new Horizon Create/Studio AI game-creation tools adds to the overhang. A high starting valuation (~80x earnings at 2025's end) left little room for error. This is a real, multi-pronged credibility/fundamentals problem, not a clean technical discount - the 52-week-high proxy is correctly flagging a story that needs real resolution (the lawsuit, AI-roadmap credibility) before being read as undervalued.

mixed

Q3 results Oct 26 after the close are the immediate test - a high-beta (~2.2) name, not a quiet bargain.

Health Care ▸
mixed

Two dated items since Oct 1. (1) Oct 12: Jefferies kept Buy but cut its target to $190 from $275, reportedly on competition concerns (Quiver Quant, AI-generated summary citing Investing.com) - consistent with the 2027 tubeless-AID competition risk below; the stock still rose ~3.3% that day. Next print expected early November. Insulet is down over 60% from its 52-week high after an August 2026 guidance cut, but management's own explanation points to a fixable operational issue rather than collapsing core demand: about two-thirds of the cut traced to weaker type-2 diabetes customer retention and utilization in the first 90 days of therapy, with the remainder from slower new-customer starts and pricing mix - not competitive share loss. The real risk ahead is that tubeless automated-insulin-delivery competitors are expected to enter the market in 2027, which could pressure both share and pricing. Value case depends on retention tools (Omnipod Discover) fixing the 90-day drop-off before competition arrives.
